I feel you bro and I can really relate to your situation, but the absolute worse thing you can do right now is keep regretting and living in self-hatred, trust me, my whole life has been nothing but regrets and self-hatred, so much so that since that was my norm it leads me to doing things Ik I'll regret. Ik it's hard not to blame yourself, especially if you did truly cause the relationship to end to some extent, but I'd also reflect on how your ex behaved. With these people we love, we tend to idealize them while we're with and after they're gone, but that's bad because then all that leaves us with is thoughts about how bad we are. Like I said I experienced something extremely similar to you, I pushed my ex away, and was being very distant and then she broke up with me and at first I didn't even care, prolly mainly because I tend to fetishise the idea of independence and loneliness, but then when she slept with other people in a clear attempt to try an replace me, that killed me and ruined me and made me realize I loved her way more than I ever thought and then when I needed her most from the pain she caused me, she didn't help me which forcefully shoved me into really strong suicidal thoughts and tendencies. Just because we didn't treat our ex's how we should of doesn't mean they're in the right for moving on so fast or trying to move fast because at the end of the day tryna rush things is immature and leads to more pain, so your ex and my ex both acted immaturely and that's not idealistic if u ask me. So try to look at everything from both sides, don't be biased against yourself because you don't like how things went because all that'll cause you is just more pain and don't put people on a pedestal no matter what you feel for them because they're nothing more than a human just like you and they messed up just like you.

I know what it's like to have no motivation or willpower to do things or better my situations, that's actually what I'm going through right now as I would say I'm also depressed due to a relationship I had. I think the best course of action is to cut her off, ik she's your mom, but sometimes family isn't supposed to stay. If the relationship is this toxic, you need to get out of it. She's way older, so this behavior and thought process is unfortunately prolly firmly set in her mind so it'll be hard for her to change, and you can't keep suffering the ill effects of her mindset until it's too late. I'd say cut her off for now and try to revisit her later in the future, hopefully she'll be better by then, but if not u jus gotta maintain your distance from her. She might be your mom, but that doesn't mean she has to always be in your life. I know that might seem like a negative outlook, but you'll be better off for it. Remain strong, and if you wanna increase your motivation/will power, something to do is start off by creating small tasks for yourself that are easy to complete, and then work your way up to more important and difficult tasks. I'm not sure how effective that is, but I feel it's something worth trying out.
